name: relvato-security
description: WordPress security monitoring your AI assistant can run: known-vulnerable plugins, themes and core, tampered files, unexpected admin accounts and sign-ins, signs of a hack, and sensitive files left public. Add a site, run the security monitors, read the findings and get the fix, with safe plugin updates and quarantine mode after a hack. The outside checks work on any website.

interface.longDescription:
Relvato Security Monitoring watches your WordPress sites for the things that turn into a breach. Through the Relvato WordPress plugin it reads the site from inside: plugins, themes and WordPress core with known vulnerabilities (most urgent when a flaw is being exploited right now), core, plugin and theme files that changed when nothing should have, admin accounts and sign-ins you didn't expect, and stale backups. From the outside it looks for signs of a hack, such as spam pages and redirects served only to Google, scripts loaded from places they shouldn't be, and sensitive files left public, like backups, .env and config files or leaked keys. Those outside checks work on any website, WordPress or not. Monitors run on a schedule and again every time the site changes.

This app brings your Relvato account's security monitoring into ChatGPT. Sign in once, then ask in plain words:
- "Has my WordPress site been hacked, or does it have a vulnerable plugin?"
- "Which of my WordPress plugins have known vulnerabilities?"
- "Are any backups, config files or keys exposed on my site?"
- "Who signed in to my WordPress admin recently?"

What ChatGPT can do with it:
- Set up: add a site, walk you through connecting the Relvato WordPress plugin (or a DNS record for other sites), and add the security monitors.
- Read: the site's security verdict and briefing, each run's findings, the brief for fixing them, WordPress plugin updates and the activity log.
- Act: run the security monitors now, get a safe update for a vulnerable plugin or the one fix a run proposes, applied by an administrator in WordPress, and start quarantine mode after a hack: hourly security runs for 48 hours with plugin updates paused.
- Review: ignore a finding you confirm is expected, or report one that's wrong. Every such decision can be undone.

You stay in control. Tools that change your site are marked so ChatGPT asks you first, and ChatGPT never ignores a security finding on its own judgement. It works within your Relvato account's limits and can't skip proving a site is yours. Approving file or script changes, stopping quarantine, choosing who receives alerts, secrets, deleting data and billing stay in the Relvato dashboard.

Sign-in uses your Relvato account, and you can disconnect ChatGPT at any time under MCP connector → Connected assistants.
capabilities: Check WordPress plugins, themes and core for known vulnerabilities
Spot tampered WordPress files, unexpected admins and sign-ins
Catch signs of a hack, like spam pages only Google sees
Find sensitive files left public: backups, .env and config files, keys
Run the security monitors now and follow the results
Explain a security finding and how to fix it
Get a safe update for a vulnerable WordPress plugin
Start quarantine mode after a WordPress hack
Review WordPress admin sign-ins and account changes
defaultPrompt: Has my WordPress site been hacked, or does it have a vulnerable plugin?
Which of my WordPress plugins have known vulnerabilities?
Are any backups, config files or keys exposed on my site?

positive.description: Check whether the site has been hacked or has a vulnerable plugin. Expected: ChatGPT reads the site's verdict and its Security briefing, and reports what the security monitors found, with a link to each run.
positive.prompt: Has my WordPress site been hacked, or does it have a vulnerable plugin?
positive.expected_behavior: The security monitors' state (for example "No known vulnerabilities or integrity problems", or each finding with its plugin, file or account) and run links on app.relvato.com.

positive.description: Run the security monitors now and follow them. Expected: ChatGPT starts only the site's security group, says how long it takes, then reports each monitor's result.
positive.prompt: Run the security monitors on my site now and tell me what they find.
positive.expected_behavior: Confirmation that the security runs started (with an estimate and their links), then each monitor's result once finished.

positive.description: Look for sensitive files left public. Expected: ChatGPT finds the latest exposure scan and lists any exposed files (backups, .env or config files, leaked keys), or says none were found.
positive.prompt: Are any backups, config files or keys exposed on my site?
positive.expected_behavior: The latest exposure scan's result: each exposed file with why it matters and how to remove it, or that nothing sensitive was found, with the run's link.

positive.description: Explain a security finding and how to fix it. Expected: ChatGPT finds the most recent failed security run, reads its findings and the fix brief, and explains the cause and the fix. It doesn't apply anything.
positive.prompt: Explain the last security problem Relvato found on my site and how to fix it.
positive.expected_behavior: Which monitor failed and when, what it found, the likely cause and the steps to fix it, with the run's link. If no security run has failed, ChatGPT says so.

positive.description: Review recent sign-ins and account changes. Expected: ChatGPT reads the WordPress activity log and summarises administrator sign-ins and new or changed accounts.
positive.prompt: Who signed in to my WordPress admin recently, and were any accounts added?
positive.expected_behavior: A short list of recent administrator sign-ins and account changes from the activity log, or a note that the log has none.

negative.description: Approving file-integrity changes stays in the dashboard. Expected: ChatGPT may read the run, but no tool approves the change; it points the user to the run page.
negative.prompt: Approve the file integrity changes Relvato found on my site.

negative.description: Turning off quarantine mode stays in the dashboard. Expected: no tool stops quarantine; ChatGPT says it's stopped early only in the Relvato dashboard.
negative.prompt: Turn off quarantine mode on my site.

negative.description: A request unrelated to website security. Expected: no Relvato tool is called.
negative.prompt: What's a good recipe for banana bread?
